In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all four antibodies react with the same epitope--(S)APDTPAP, but that the epitopes are not identical.
all four antibodies react with the same peptide sequence SAPDTR (S = serine or threonine, P = proline, R = arginine).
the anti-peptide reactivity of these antibodies is to a peptide sequence SAPDTRPA, which is a major determinant of the MUC1 VNTr encoded epitope.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) the MUC1 protein core encoded by this gene is the antigenic target for the anti-breast and the anti-ovarian monoclonal antibodies, (2) the epitope is located within the 60 amino acid repeat, and (3) the epitope contains the amino acids PDTR.
the four antibodies react with the same peptide sequence (PDTR) but that the flanking amino acids differ, and that the epitope is 6 amino acids long (SAPDTRPAP).
the anti-MUC1 mAb reactivity is with the peptide encoded by the MUG1 gene and that the peptide is SAPDTRP, which can tolerate major changes in amino acid sequence, but not the loss of P or R.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MUC1 is a target for immunotherapy and the epitope is (S)APDT(R)P.
the epitope of anti-breast cancer mAbs is APDTR and of an anti-ovary cancer mAb DTRPA, and that these epitopes are conserved in both breast and ovarian cancer mucins.
the epitope for these mAbs is short, but flanking amino acids must be present for binding, and that the amino acids P and R are critical to binding.
